input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full. 24.1 permits Customer assignment without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets, subject only to prompt notice and assignee assumption. 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld for a capable, financially sound assignee), plus an absolute bar on assigning to a direct Customer competitor. 24.3 does not swallow 24.1 because it is expressly limited to "other assignments," operating only as a residual catch-all outside the 24.1/24.2 carve-outs, with a mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent standard. 24.4 removes any Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, closing the walk-away risk, and requires Vendor cooperation with administrative changes for a permitted successor. 13.3 tracks Section 24 by allowing licence rights to transfer to an Affiliate or successor on a permitted assignment, so a successor is not stranded. No "deemed an assignment" trap or change-of-control trigger appears elsewhere; the only other assignment reference (9.2) concerns insolvency-related general assignments for creditors. No redline needed.
